title: Q. Ports
description: `ports.json`: every dependency outside the product — a third-party API, a SaaS, payment, mail, object storage, an LLM, identity, the product's own Postgres — behind a port named by its business function, with the adapter that wraps the provider, the fake the tests and the mock-up run on, the secrets it needs (names only), its cost, and the units that use it. What the factory shows, and what a provider switch replaces.

id.description: The business function, never the provider: `payments`, `mail`, `object-storage`, `llm`, `identity`, `database`.

purpose.description: What the product needs from outside, in a sentence.

stateful.description: The provider keeps state (a customer, a file, a user). Our Data is the truth: only DataCapabilities write through it, and Capabilities read our mirror, never the provider.

name.description: The SDK, crate, package or API: `stripe-rust`, `aws-sdk-s3`, `sqlx`, `api.mailgun.net v3`.

adapter.description: The real adapter's crate, relative to the root: `crates/ports/payments/stripe`.

fake.description: The fake every test, the rules' runtime and the mock-up run on: `crates/ports/payments` (its `fake` module). Postgres has none: it runs in Docker.

secrets.description: The secrets it needs, by name, never their values: kept encrypted with sops in `secrets/<env>.enc.yaml`.

cost.description: How it is paid, its quotas: `per transaction, 1.5% + 0.25€`.

usedBy.description: The Capabilities (reads, stateless ports only) and DataCapabilities (writes) that name it in their manifests' `ports`.
